_schema: Decode (TPOT) wall-time progression vs roofline. Iteration metric = perf-proxy (4-layer dummy) B=32 decode tok/s. Roofline = decode BW ceiling (MoE weight-streaming); baseline ~= 75% of 226 GB/s. IMPORTANT: in-engine decode tok/s is CONFIG-UNSTABLE (off swings 24/48/81/90 with mem-fraction + ~10% run-to-run at a FIXED config), so deltas MUST come from a CONTROLLED HELD-FIXED A/B (off vs on, same job, same config, adjacent), NOT a sequential multi-config bisection.
metric: proxy B=32 decode tok/s — FULL-NODE (all NUMA domains, 128c), the max-throughput config; single-NUMA per-rank = 32 tok/s (BW-bound, 2.8x lower)
ceiling_label: decode BW roofline — MoE weight-streaming at full-node (all 3 SNC NUMA domains / 128c); the gap is the ~40% compute-bound torch DSA/MHC decode ops, not pure BW loss

retracted_regression.note: An earlier sequential 7-config bisection (jobs 386002/386010) reported compressor 21.4 + sinkhorn 21.2 vs off 81.7 -- a ~3.8x REGRESSION. RETRACTED: it did not reproduce in a controlled held-fixed off-vs-on A/B at THREE configs. Root cause = MEASUREMENT ARTIFACT: in-engine decode tok/s is config-unstable (3x swing with mem-fraction, ~10% run-to-run) and the sequential multi-config bisection drifted across 7 heavy engine inits (off itself read 81.7 in the bisection vs 90.0 in the controlled A/B at the SAME 0.85 config). Lesson: validate the instrument with a controlled adjacent A/B before concluding an in-engine regression; a tiny op showing a large E2E 'regression' is a red flag to check the instrument FIRST.
